target.title: fix(config): use Object.hasOwn for own-key checks in write-prepare helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createMergePatch`, `collectChangedPaths`, and `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` in
`src/config/io.write-prepare.ts` use the `in` operator to test key membership
(`key in base`, `key in target`, `key in runtime`). The `in` operator walks the
entire prototype chain, so any property reachable through inheritance —
`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, or custom-prototype keys — is silently
treated as a config-owned key.

This produces three concrete failure modes:

1. **`createMergePatch`:** inherited keys appear in the output patch, injecting
   non-existent config fields into the write candidate.
2. **`collectChangedPaths`:** inherited keys are reported as changed paths,
   triggering spurious write-prepare work and incorrect diff sets.
3. **`projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape`:** authored source keys whose names collide
   with inherited property names are incorrectly skipped (the `!(key in runtime)`
   guard short-circuits before reaching the authored value).

## Why This Change Was Made

`Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the correct primitive for "does this specific object
have this key, ignoring its prototype chain." It is available in all Node.js versions
the project supports (Node 16.9+, present as standard since ES2022). Replacing five
`key in obj` guards with `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` closes all three failure modes in
one bounded change with no surface-area growth.

## User Impact

**Before:** config objects that inherit from a non-null prototype (e.g. objects created
with `Object.create(someProto)`, or objects whose prototype happens to carry own
properties named after config keys) produce incorrect merge patches, spurious changed-
path sets, and silently dropped authored source keys.

**After:** only the object's own keys are considered in all three helpers. Inherited
keys are ignored; authored keys whose names collide with prototype property names are
preserved correctly.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/fix-io-write-prepare-hasown`
Base: `upstream/main` (`9c08808bd7`)
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when building merge patches 1ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > preserves authored keys whose names match Object.prototype members 0ms
 ✓ config io write prepare > ignores prototype-chain keys when collecting changed paths 0ms
 ... (48 pre-existing tests also pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
   Duration  140ms
```

Three new regression tests cover each fixed function directly:

- `createMergePatch` with an object whose prototype has own properties → only own key `safe` appears in the patch
- `projectSourceOntoRuntimeShape` with a source key named `toString` → authored value is preserved, not skipped
- `collectChangedPaths` with prototype-bearing objects → only the own key `safe.mode` is reported as changed

### Diff summary

```
src/config/io.write-prepare.ts      |  6 +-  (5 key-in → Object.hasOwn replacements)
src/config/io.write-prepare.test.ts | 54 ++  (3 new regression cases)
```

### Format check

```
$ git diff --check
(no output — clean)
```

### What was not tested

Live `openclaw configure` / `openclaw doctor --fix` round-trip against a real
`openclaw.json` file with a prototype-bearing config object. The fix is
mechanical — five identical `in` → `Object.hasOwn` substitutions — and the
three regression tests directly exercise all affected code paths. Crabbox/Testbox
remote CI was not available at submission time.
